title: AI Studio: three neural networks, 2 MB of weights, streamed from the DDR
summary: All three AIs in one FPGA design, and much bigger: the weights live in the board's 512 MB DDR memory and stream into the FPGA through two HP ports while a network runs, about 100 times faster than the ARM. Read digits with a reader 10 times bigger, let a text model with 32 letters of memory write, draw sharper digits, and teach the reader your own handwriting.

slots.1: DDR network engine (weights in the DDR, 2 HP ports, its own 75 MHz clock)

parts: nothing: everything happens inside the FPGA and the board's memory
tested: the self-test passed 9 of 9 checks on the real board (October 2026): the reader, the text model and the drawer streamed from the DDR, every output equal to the Python integer math, no DDR errors, 50 of 50 test digits; about 100 times faster than numpy on the ARM. Learn my handwriting tried end to end.
